channel.title: EcoCompute — Notes
channel.description: Evidence-based notes on the energy cost of LLM inference, from direct NVML GPU power measurements.

item.title: Re-running a number we didn't trust: 89% of the session was cooldown
item.description: A protocol note on redoing an energy measurement we had published as a probable overestimate. Four fixes: a forced cooldown to idle before every run (all 45 converged, each starting at 24-28 W and 27-29 C), randomized run order under a fixed seed, --ignore-eos so every run decodes its full target, and NVML's hardware energy counter in place of an integrated power trace. What each one changed: --ignore-eos moved the headline 1.7 points to -61.9%, the cooldown inverted the power conclusion (the quantized arms draw 296-319 W against F16's 273 W, not the same), a third output length turned the differencing assumption into a tested one (E = a + b*n fits at R2 above 0.9966 with intercepts of 171-378 J), and the counter reads 14.9% higher than trapezoidal integration of the same run's 100 Hz trace, range 2.5-31.8%, falling to 0.2-4.3% after differencing. Cost: 50 minutes of one rented RTX 4090, of which 5.4 were compute and 45.1 were waiting for the card to cool. Still open: token counts are inferred from --ignore-eos and rc=0 rather than read back from llama.cpp's timing line, and perplexity was not re-measured. Data archived at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22295184.

item.title: It was never the format. It's the kernel.
item.description: Corrected 2026-09-03. MLPerf Client v2.0 ships an already-quantized suite, so it cannot tell you what quantization cost. We measured the missing FP16 baseline inside one runtime: on an RTX 4090, llama.cpp GGUF Q4_0 decoding Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct costs 61.9% less energy per token than GGUF F16 for +5.60% perplexity (45 runs, n=5 per cell, three token lengths, randomized order, forced cooldown before every run, NVML hardware energy counter, decode-only by differencing 576- and 64-token cells with the linearity checked at R2 above 0.996). The quantized arms draw MORE power than F16, 296-319 W against 273 W, and win purely on throughput (2.8-3.2x). On the same card, bitsandbytes LLM.int8() costs 106% MORE energy per token and NF4 saves 39%: three weight-only quantizations of a 7-8B model spanning +106% to -62%, so the bit width does not predict the sign, the kernel does. Our own Q4_0 file and the one MLPerf Client v2.0 ships are indistinguishable (final PPL 7.7364 vs 7.7366, max per-chunk difference 0.0003 over 564 chunks), which is published as a zero result, not as a win. The first pass, published 2026-08-31, reported -63.6% and was flagged as a likely overestimate; it was, by about 1.7 points, and the superseded CSV stays published. Still not an MLPerf result: GPU-package power, no MLCommons review, token counts inferred from --ignore-eos rather than read back, and perplexity carried over from the first session. Data archived at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22295184.

item.title: The first independent replication: NF4 saved 16% on a laptop GPU
item.description: The first energy.json contributed by someone other than the maintainer: TinyLlama-1.1B in NF4 on an RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU, direct NVML, n=1. It saves 16.2% energy at a size where every card in our own set spends 4.6-33% more, and it is the lowest absolute energy per token we have on record for that model. The fitted Ampere curve is extrapolated six-fold below its 7-14B anchors there, so its honest band is about +/-30 points - the submission page now says that instead of claiming a contradiction. The paired perplexity, 10.1016 against an FP16 9.6201, reproduces our own RTX 4090 measurement to four decimals: quality travels between machines, energy does not. Contributed points are drawn but never fitted.

item.title: How repeatable is a quantization energy number?
item.description: Five INT8 configurations re-run three times each on one RTX 4090 (n=3, direct NVML). The coefficient of variation of the FP16-normalised energy delta is 0.6-3.9% and of the raw joules 0.3-2.0%, so the 100-140 percentage point gap between two of our own sessions is 30-50x the run-to-run noise and cannot be sampling. The gap is entirely a throughput effect at unchanged package power; the leading hypothesis, untested, is the LLM.int8() kernel path differing between torch 2.13.0 in the image and torch 2.5.1+cu121 natively. Absolute joules also drifted 12-17% lower overnight on the same host. Data: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22037483.

item.title: Energy and quality, measured in the same run
item.description: Ten RTX 4090 configurations whose decode energy and perplexity come from the same run (direct NVML, n=1 each). NF4 saves 39% energy at 7B but costs 12% perplexity; INT8 costs about 0.5% perplexity and never saves energy. A delta-perplexity filter of 1% rejects every NF4 row and admits nearly every INT8 one, inverting the energy ranking. Also reports a 2.0-2.5x cross-session discrepancy in the INT8 penalty on the same card model and software stack. Data: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22037483.

item.title: We ran our own container on a rented RTX 4090: NF4 breaks even just above 3B, INT8 lost at every size we tested
item.description: 15 of 15 configurations measured with direct NVML on a rented RTX 4090 using our own open MLCube container. NF4 flips from a +36% penalty at 0.5B to break-even at 3B and a -28% saving at 7B; INT8 cost more energy at all five sizes tested (n=1 each, bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) because decode throughput collapses to 9-19 tok/s. Data archived at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22037483.

item.title: When not to quantize: the small-model energy penalty
item.description: Weight-only NF4/INT8 quantization shrinks memory but can raise LLM inference energy by 25–55% for small models. What 360+ real GPU measurements show about the crossover point, and when quantization is still the right call.
